chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the selling of the Mushaf (copies of the Quran), he said: 'Do not sell the Book (of Quran), nor buy it, but sell the paper, the leather, and the iron.'

key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: The Book, referring specifically to the Quran in this context
key_terms.الْمَصَاحِفِ: Plural of Mushaf, referring to copies of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling copies of the Quran in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of distinguishing between the sacred text and its physical medium, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding the commercialization of the Quran. The Imam’s instruction to sell the paper, leather, and iron rather than the 'book' itself reflects the view that the Mushaf is a vessel of reverence, not a mere commodity for trade. This ruling underscores the spiritual value of the Quran, ensuring it is treated with dignity rather than reduced to a marketable good.
